title: ToStringMapIntE/ToStringMapInt64E panic on maps with non-string keys
property: for any map input the function returns a result or an error, never panics; key count is preserved on success
expected: map[string]int{"0": 0} (keys converted like the map[any]T case uses ToString) or at least a non-nil error
actual: panic: reflect.Value.SetMapIndex: value of type int is not assignable to type string (map.go:191)
evidence: The function is an E-variant that returns an error for uncastable input; the reflect fallback is explicitly meant to accept arbitrary map kinds, and sibling ToStringMapStringE returns an error (not a panic) for map[int]string. The map[any]T and map[any]any branches convert keys with ToString, but the reflect fallback passes the original key to SetMapIndex.

title: ToStringMapStringSliceE treats map[any]string values differently from map[string]string
property: map[any]string{k: v} and map[string]string{k: v} convert to the same map[string][]string
expected: map["k":["a b"]], same as the map[string]string case, which wraps each string value in a one-element slice
actual: map["k":["a" "b"]]; and for value "" the result is an empty slice instead of [""]
evidence: The map[string]string branch does m[k] = []string{val}; the map[any]string branch calls ToStringSlice(val), which whitespace-splits the string, so equivalent inputs give different outputs and strings with spaces are split / empty strings dropped.
